query: Write a design doc on the tradeoffs between io_uring and epoll for a high-throughput proxy.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/document-reasoning.md, reference/amazon-writing.md, and reference/prose-profile.md before drafting
States the requested decision, audience, recommendation, and scope before selecting sections
Builds sections from reader questions and decision risks rather than copying a default template
Gathers real figures (syscall counts, benchmark numbers, kernel versions) before writing prose
Defines unfamiliar terms before a heading, diagram, or claim depends on them
Derives evaluation criteria from requirements before comparing io_uring and epoll
Produces zero em-dashes
Uses 'For example' and 'such as' followed by named instances, at least twice combined
Names at least two options, states which is chosen and why
Volunteers a cost in the same paragraph as each claimed benefit
Runs scripts/check_style.py and iterates until it exits 0
Contains no data-platform or financial vocabulary from the derivation corpus

query: Here is a draft section I wrote. Check it against my style and fix what is off.
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/check_style.py on the draft first rather than eyeballing it
Reports the specific measured deviations, not a general impression
Fixes hard failures (em-dashes, banned tokens, second person, RFC uppercase modals)
Does not flatten sentence-length variance while fixing other issues
Re-runs the checker after editing to confirm it exits 0

query: Draft a one-pager proposing we move our metrics pipeline from cron to an event-driven trigger.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/document-types/one-pager.md and keeps implementation detail below HLD altitude
Uses only sections needed for the decision and may merge context, problem, or scope
Opens with the decision, recommendation, decisive reasons, principal downside, and reversibility
Separates scenario constraints, verified facts, and assumptions
Compares the proposal, status quo, and strongest credible alternative against common criteria
Paragraph lengths vary, including at least one single-sentence paragraph
Does not produce uniformly 3-4 sentence paragraphs
Sentence lengths spread with sd >= 9 and at least one sentence over 40 words
Includes calibrated hedges for anything not under the author's control
Leaves at least one claim explicitly unresolved
Records reversibility of the decision
Ends on a technical fact rather than a summary paragraph

query: Write a PRFAQ for a service that creates an isolated preview environment for each code review. The customer is an application team currently sharing one integration environment.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/document-types/prfaq.md and reference/document-types/prfaq-sections.md
Selects FAQ questions from customer and investment risks instead of reproducing every reference subsection
Keeps the press release focused on the customer problem and future experience rather than architecture
Separates the press release, external FAQ, and internal FAQ
Addresses cost allocation, secrets, data restrictions, quotas, operations, support, success metrics, and stop conditions
Labels hypothetical quotes and does not invent customer evidence
Includes difficult unanswered questions rather than writing around them

query: Write an LLD for idempotency keys in a payment API. Concurrent requests with the same key and different payloads must not both succeed, and the downstream payment may commit before our response is stored.
expected_behavior: Reads reference/document-types/lld.md, lld-contracts.md, and lld-delivery.md
Organizes around the component's unresolved implementation decisions rather than a fixed LLD outline
Links or states inherited HLD decisions without repeating a business case
Defines request contracts, payload validation, key scope, state transitions, concurrency, timeout, retry, and recovery behavior
Maps invariants and failure modes to tests and operational signals
Covers migration, mixed versions, launch, rollback, and cleanup where relevant
Avoids cataloging every class or method

query: Run a rigorous writer and judge workflow on a random technical design topic. Keep revising until an independent panel accepts it.
expected_behavior: Loads agent-sops/iterative-technical-doc-review.sop.md and reference/review-rubric.md
Selects a topic from evaluations/topic-bank.json and distinguishes scenario constraints from verified facts
Creates an evidence pack and two independent candidate drafts
Uses fresh isolated critics for revision rounds
Runs scripts/check_style.py before panel review
Dispatches independent argument, technical, and document judges
Uses scripts/aggregate_review_panel.py and accepts only on unanimous votes, threshold scores, no blockers, and a passing style check
Stops at finite limits and reports NOT_ACCEPTED when blockers remain
